entities.text: High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard Mr. Randhir Kumar, learned counsel for the appellant and Mr. Rakesh Ranjan, learned A.P.P.
This application has been preferred by the appellant for grant of bail to him during the pendency of this appeal.

The appellant has been convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 304B and 498A IPC and has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for ten years for the offence under Section 304B IPC.
It has been alleged that the daughter of the informant had died in unnatural circumstances at her matrimonial house.

Learned counsel for the appellant had submitted that the appellant is the husband of the deceased and the evidence of the parents'-in-law of the appellant, who have been examined as P.W.1 and P.W.7 categorically reveal that the relationship between the appellant and the deceased was cordial.

It has further been submitted that the post mortem report indicates the cause of death as asphyxia Binod Kr. Singh @ Binod Singh vs The State Of Jharkhand on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183690760/
1 due to hanging and there is a possibility of suicidal hanging as well.

entities.text: Binod Kr. Singh @ Binod Singh vs The State Of Jharkhand on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: No injuries were found on the person of the deceased.
Learned A.P.P. has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant.
On consideration of the evidence of P.W.1 and P.W.7 apart from the post mortem report, we are inclined to admit the appellant on bail.

Accordingly, during pendency of this appeal, the appellant is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.10,000/- (Ten thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge-II, FTC (CAW), Bermo at Tenughat in S.T. No. No. 29/2023.
